svg.title: Sequential, strided, and random access versus cache-line use
svg.desc: Three address streams over 64-byte cache lines show sequential access consuming all eight 8-byte elements, a 64-byte stride consuming one element per fetched line, and dependent random access both wasting line bytes and serializing next-address discovery.
svg.text: A 64-byte fill is useful only if its neighbors are consumed

g.text: * A0 * A1 * A2 * A3 * A4 * A5 * A6 * A7 - 64 / 64 bytes used

svg.text: One line fill supports eight adjacent accesses; prefetch and overlap are possible.
Stride = 64 bytes: one 8-byte element from each line
Each orange block is 8 useful bytes in a different fetched line: 8 / 64 bytes used per line.
Dependent random chain: A[5] -> A[91] -> A[2] -> A[700]
The next address is unavailable until the current load completes: latency is exposed.
Working-set size still matters: random access can be fast when all lines remain nearby.
